question: Does a separately compiled pure finite-source validator reduce exact production-route CPU cost on all ten retained startup inputs?
baseline: Unchanged original recursive GDScript validator, with the same outer policy dispatch
expected_helper_build: Release build with godot 0.5.4, minimal bindings and API 4.7; independently retained image, original controller DLL unchanged
required_correctness: All malformed/type/depth/cycle controls match the original oracle
Exact full route output for every repetition
No physics construction, solver step or native physics read
Unchanged source/runtime bindings and owned cleanup

timing.sample: Thirty warm route timings per policy family per packet, excluding repeat zero in each reused-cache block
timing.packet_reduction_fraction: 1 - median(native_first + native_second warm samples) / median(original_first + original_second warm samples)
timing.cohort_statistic: Unweighted median of the ten packet reduction fractions
timing.fresh_cache: Retained secondary diagnostic only; not used to choose a different outcome
timing.function_timers: Inclusive and overlapping; never sum nested costs

promotion: Passing this CPU diagnostic permits a separately qualified, clean pushed matched native timing successor; it does not adopt a default or establish native speedup
performance_comparison_scope: Exact retained one-body one-seed startup corpus; no startup distribution, robustness or real-time claim
